books.section: Topic 6.12 Controversies over the Role of Government in the Gilded Age

stimulus.text:
Government and the railroads:

| Year | Event |
| 1877 | In Munn v. Illinois, the Supreme Court upholds an Illinois law setting maximum charges for grain storage, ruling that property used in a way that affects the public may be regulated. |
| 1886 | In Wabash v. Illinois, the Supreme Court rules that a state may not regulate railroad rates on shipments crossing state lines. |
| 1887 | Congress passes the Interstate Commerce Act, creating the Interstate Commerce Commission to regulate railroads. The Act requires that railroad charges “shall be reasonable and just.” |
| 1897 | In the Maximum Rate Case, the Supreme Court rules that the Interstate Commerce Commission may not set railroad rates. |
stimulus.source_note: Munn v. Illinois, 94 U.S. 113 (1877); Wabash, St. Louis and Pacific Railway Co. v. Illinois, 118 U.S. 557 (1886); Interstate Commerce Act, February 4, 1887, Section 1 (quoted clause exact); Interstate Commerce Commission v. Cincinnati, New Orleans and Texas Pacific Railway Co., 167 U.S. 479 (1897), the Maximum Rate Case.

stem: What pattern does the table show across the years 1877 to 1897?

options.text: Each step toward regulation was followed by a narrowing decision
The courts steadily widened federal power over the economy
options.misconception: Wabash and the Maximum Rate Case narrowed regulation, so power did not steadily widen.

options.text: Congress never passed any law about railroad rates at all
options.misconception: Congress passed the Interstate Commerce Act in 1887.

options.text: The states kept full power to regulate railroads throughout
options.misconception: Wabash took state power over interstate rates away in 1886.

rationales.A: Munn allowed regulation, Wabash limited the states, and the Maximum Rate Case limited the Commission.
rationales.B: Wabash and the Maximum Rate Case narrowed power, so it did not steadily widen.
rationales.C: The Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 was a federal railroad law.
rationales.D: Wabash barred the states from regulating interstate railroad rates in 1886.
rationales.general:
Read the rows as one story.
1. Munn in 1877 allowed the states to regulate a business affecting the public.
2. Wabash in 1886 took state power over interstate railroad rates away.
3. Congress answered with the Interstate Commerce Act in 1887.
4. The Maximum Rate Case in 1897 then limited the new Commission itself.
Remember: in this period, regulation advanced one step and the courts pulled it back.
